It LOOKS like a believable billing form, but no input is * validated against real card rules, nothing is sent over the * network, and nothing is persisted anywhere. * * Stage 2 ("revealed"): entered only after the participant clicks * "Subscribe". Immediately explains this was the simulation and * walks through the red flags, including the ones specific to a fake * checkout/payment form. */ const RED_FLAGS = [ 'Urgency and scarcity in the ad — "before it expires", "first 50 students" — designed to get you clicking before you think.', 'A reward disproportionate to anything you actually did, for a service you never signed up for.', 'A checkout page that asks for a full card number, expiry and CVC before you have any real relationship with the brand.', 'A believable-looking plan/pricing layout is easy to fake — visual polish is not proof a page is legitimate.', 'No way to verify you are even on the real domain for "Lumen AI Assistant" — a lookalike site can be built in minutes.', ]; export default function AdLanding() { const navigate = useNavigate(); const [stage, setStage] = useState('checkout'); const [plan, setPlan] = useState('monthly'); const handleSubscribe = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); // Intentionally does nothing with the form data — it is never read, // sent, or stored. Only the stage changes. setStage('revealed'); }; if (stage === 'revealed') { return (
